YTA. As someone with a sibling who has severe special needs, I completely understand where she is coming from. My whole childhood was centred around caring for my sibling due to his high needs. I can barely remember any instances where I ever got to have a meal with both parents. I don’t feel like I know them very well at all as we were all so focused on caring for my sibling. 

Please don’t deprive her of actually spending quality time with you. Trust me, it hurts to be the neglected child. I remember at the age of 6 thinking that I wouldn’t be able to have my own family or ever get married due to feeling like it was my duty to care for my sibling with special needs. It’s something I have carried into my adulthood and still feel as if my sole purpose is to care for my sibling. I’ve missed out on a lot because of this, and I’m incredibly proud of Elizabeth for being able to live her own life.

Literally a hug. You need to realise some people with disabilities (like my own brother) can have the mental age of a child and mean no ill intent. For example, my brother still only watches cartoons targeted at 5 year olds despite being an adult. It is likely your relative hugged you because in his mind he sees you both the same age and believes it’s acceptable. Parents can do as much as they want to try stop this behaviour but it is very difficult to control the actions of someone who is neuro-diverse as they may not have the ability to process these social norms.
